doc.title: Al Vollmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, June 8, 2017

title: Record collecting and research at Hamilton
summary: He did no concert promotion, collected records and learned thesis research, wanting to find out who played on records.

bands.name: Sidney De Paris and Wilbur De Paris band

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: So did you get a taste of Hamilton, did you do any concert promotion or anything like —

No. I did nothing. At that time I didn’t have a whole lot of money. I was barely getting by although I can’t say I ever suffered any hardship. But I was more collecting, I was more learning, I was reading, I was, I even bid on some records. I was more of a record collector. Now what I learned at Hamilton was how to write a thesis or, you know, with footnotes, and go to sources and all of that, which stood me in good stead later. Because later I wrote some articles and also I did research. But my interest at that time was very much focused on who’s playing what on the records. And I felt a certain responsibility, being European and being here in America where the musicians were. Because in Europe all we could do was put a record on and then put the other record on and say, “Doesn’t this trumpeter sound like the same guy.” Whereas I had access to the musicians. Because quite early on, by going to Jimmy Ryan’s and being knocked out by the Sidney DeParis- Wilbur DeParis aggregation, I got to know Hayes Alvis, the bass player. And he was living alone.
